memory_update.text: COHR and LITE should be retained as reference leaders for AI InP photonics, lasers, and data-center optical components; they anchor the node but are not the primary underfollowed alpha lane.

VECO is a high-priority underfollowed Layer 1B candidate because official company evidence directly links its MOCVD, ion-beam deposition, and wet-processing orders to InP laser manufacturing and optical interconnect demand.
ALMU may remain in the speculative shadow lane only if later filings confirm commercial AI photonics or communications customers, wafer-scale manufacturability, and repeat revenue.
Need a follow-up pass on US-listed optical test, wafer bonding, photodetector, and inspection suppliers; current evidence is strongest for lasers/InP device makers and MOCVD/IBD equipment.

node: Compound semiconductor photonics, InP substrates, CPO, lasers, photodetectors, epitaxy, etch and bonding equipment
summary: Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe around the AI optical-interconnect and compound-photonics chokepoint. The clearest direct-exposure names are Coherent and Lumentum as InP photonics and AI data-center optical component leaders. Veeco enters the underfollowed equipment lane because recent company disclosures tie its MOCVD, ion-beam deposition, and wet-processing tools directly to InP laser manufacturing and silicon-photonics optical interconnect demand. Aeluma is included only as a speculative shadow candidate because its III-V-on-silicon platform could be relevant if native InP wafer capacity remains constrained, but commercial qualification, revenue scale, customer concentration, and manufacturability require verification.
